name: uses a patch bump even when the selected fix has a minor changeset
reason: The first cold Changesets CLI launch exceeded 5 seconds in two merge groups. Keep all cold CLI integration cases in this lane so selection cannot move the failure to the next case.
removeWhen: Fix cold CLI startup and pass ten independent runs without prewarming or increasing the 5 second allowance.

name: keeps the real fixed group in sync and preserves extension SDK and UI ranges
reason: Shares the cold Changesets CLI path with the failing merge-group test; also owns the no-contributor-changeset contract formerly duplicated by the small fixture.
removeWhen: Fix cold CLI startup and pass ten independent runs within the existing 5 second allowance.

name: packaged editing sessions preview, coalesce saves and cancel gestures in chromium
reason: Preview intermittently retains position 0,0 after reload instead of 12,24; Firefox and WebKit remain blocking. Retain first-attempt trace and source-canvas assertions.
removeWhen: Reproduce and fix preview state propagation after reload, then pass ten independent Chromium runs without retries.

name: packaged editing sessions preview, coalesce saves and cancel gestures in webkit
reason: The initial editing deep link intermittently lands on project Home in WebKit, so no editing frame exists. The same compiled code passes in other first-attempt runs. Retain the failed navigation trace; Firefox remains blocking.
removeWhen: Reproduce and fix initial extension-route restoration in WebKit, then pass ten independent WebKit runs without retries.

name: persists commands and settings through authenticated opaque webviews in WebKit (Safari engine)
reason: WebKit intermittently retains a visible settings dialog after its close button is activated. The same fixture passes in other independent runs and other engines. Preserve the existing close and reload assertions and first-attempt trace.
removeWhen: Reproduce and fix the WebKit settings-close lifecycle, then pass ten independent WebKit runs without retries.

name: opens and closes project tabs while preserving pages and terminals
reason: One Apple Silicon cold startup consumed about 18 seconds of this 30 second lifecycle test; it timed out at the first Lab frame at 30.434 seconds. The same commit passed at 15.719 seconds in another native job. Keep Linux, Windows and Intel coverage blocking.
removeWhen: Identify and fix the slow phase and pass ten independent Apple Silicon runs within 30 seconds, preserving cold startup and all lifecycle assertions.

name: the owner can reconcile conflicting dependencies and submit without a human request
reason: On Windows this case exhausted its 15 second allowance in one PR run; on the same branch it took 3.0 to 6.6 seconds. The case before it in the same file took 13.9 seconds instead of 2.3, so the whole Windows runner was slow. The case runs many git commands to build and reconcile a conflicting stack.
removeWhen: Find the slow git phase of the conflicting-stack fixture on Windows and fix it, then pass ten independent Windows runs within the existing 15 second allowance.

name: the packaged Codex harness preserves protocol loss and independent provider failure
reason: The Windows cold compiled-runtime fixture intermittently exhausts 30 seconds after its runtime becomes ready at 8.8 seconds. The same case completes on other independent Windows runs. Preserve both protocol and provider-failure assertions.
removeWhen: Identify and fix the slow phase, then pass ten independent Windows runs within the existing 30 second allowance, without retries.

name: installs the smoke browser without external JavaScript runtimes
reason: The Windows packaged browser installs successfully, then intermittently fails to finish browser validation and cleanup within 30 seconds. Other independent Windows runs pass. Preserve the empty-PATH installation and real Chromium page checks.
removeWhen: Identify and fix the slow phase, then pass ten independent Windows runs within the existing 30 second allowance, without retries.

name: the installed Playwright cache runs a packaged extension page outside the checkout
reason: Shares the Windows packaged browser validation path with the quarantined smoke-browser case and exhausted its 30 seconds in the same way. Preserve the outside-checkout cache and real page checks.
removeWhen: Identify and fix the slow phase, then pass ten independent Windows runs within the existing 30 second allowance, without retries.

name: preserves conversation history before the persisted queued follow-up prompt
reason: One Windows first-attempt run exhausted the fixture's 30 status polls before the harness completion was persisted. Other independent runs passed. Keep the conversation ordering and queued follow-up assertions and the existing test limit.
removeWhen: Fix completion synchronization and pass ten independent Windows runs at the existing limits.

name: refreshes local default extensions when an existing project starts in source mode
reason: On Windows the restarted test app did not refresh the installed default extension within the fixture's 10 second wait in one merge-queue run; the same code passed this shard on a later full run and passes on macOS and Linux. Keep the restart and refresh assertions and add phase logs to find the slow step.
removeWhen: Identify and fix the slow refresh step, then pass ten independent Windows runs within the existing 10 second wait.

name: refreshes local default extensions when running from source
reason: On Windows the fixture's temp folder could not be removed after the test app closed (EPERM), even with five delete retries; a rerun of the same job passed. A file inside the folder stays open after shutdown. Keep the cleanup and find which handle survives `close()`.
removeWhen: Find and close the handle that outlives app shutdown, then pass ten independent Windows runs.

name: counts a program that replaces the interactive shell
reason: In one Linux merge group the supervisor still reported the shell as idle 100 ms after `exec sleep 5` was written: the prompt marker had been read but the DEBUG-trap busy marker had not. It did not reproduce on macOS or on Linux with 0.3 CPUs. Keep the replaced-shell assertion.
removeWhen: Make the test wait for the busy marker instead of a fixed 100 ms, or fix the reader lag it exposes, then pass ten independent Linux runs.

name: detaches its image after the volume is unmounted
reason: On Intel macOS runners, `diskutil unmount force` on the owned fixture volume intermittently does not return after the image attaches, so the case exhausts 10 seconds. It failed five merge groups whose changes do not touch the desktop client; Apple Silicon remains blocking. Preserve the forced-unmount precondition and the detach assertions.
removeWhen: Find why the forced unmount stalls on Intel runners, fix it, then pass ten independent darwin-x64 runs within the existing 10 second allowance.

name: restores each project's navigation order, placement, and visibility after relaunch
reason: Apple Silicon exhausted 30 seconds across two app launches while reopening the second project after relaunch; no runtime error was logged. The merge group changed only extension manifests and report bodies. Keep Linux, Windows and Intel coverage blocking.
removeWhen: Identify and fix the slow phase and pass ten independent Apple Silicon runs within 30 seconds, preserving both launches and all navigation assertions.

name: keeps a navigation reset after relaunch without changing another project
reason: Failed in the same Apple Silicon job with the same 30 second relaunch pattern as the order and visibility case. Keep Linux, Windows and Intel coverage blocking.
removeWhen: Identify and fix the slow phase and pass ten independent Apple Silicon runs within 30 seconds, preserving both launches and the reset assertions.

name: keeps an uncertain runtime owner intact until its descriptor is repaired
reason: On Windows this case exhausted its 60 second allowance in a merge group whose change only touches ticket numbering. The next recovery case in the same job passed. Keep Linux and macOS coverage blocking and preserve the owner-repair assertions.
removeWhen: Identify and fix the slow phase, then pass ten independent Windows runs within the existing 60 second allowance.

name: database publication waits for a temporary Windows reader to release its handle
reason: The PowerShell reader fixture never confirmed its open handle within 15 seconds; this case normally takes 2.5 to 4 seconds, mostly PowerShell startup. Later cases in the same file then received its cleanup errors. Preserve the real sharing violation and all publication assertions.
removeWhen: Replace or bound the PowerShell reader startup so a stalled reader fails fast without leaking into later cases, then pass ten independent Windows runs within the existing 15 second allowance.

name: cancelling Windows publication while a reader is open preserves the active home
reason: Shares the PowerShell reader fixture; in the same job its reader also never confirmed the open handle, and it received the previous case's cleanup errors. Preserve the real sharing violation and all publication assertions.
removeWhen: Replace or bound the PowerShell reader startup so a stalled reader fails fast without leaking into later cases, then pass ten independent Windows runs within the existing 15 second allowance.

name: a persistent Windows reader reports publication failure and preserves the active home
reason: Shares the PowerShell reader fixture; in the same job its reader never confirmed the open handle within 15 seconds, against about 0.6 seconds normally. Preserve the real sharing violation and all publication assertions.
removeWhen: Replace or bound the PowerShell reader startup so a stalled reader fails fast without leaking into later cases, then pass ten independent Windows runs within the existing 15 second allowance.

name: confirms an answer persisted during a transcript read before the turn ends
reason: On Windows this case took 19.5 seconds against its 15 second allowance in one merge group; it takes about 0.26 seconds on macOS. It writes a 32 MB transcript and appends while the first read is in flight, so the slow phase is the large file write or read on the Windows runner. Keep the in-flight append assertion.
removeWhen: Identify the slow phase of the 32 MB transcript fixture on Windows and fix it, then pass ten independent Windows runs within the existing 15 second allowance.

name: packaged Planner recovers missing workspaces without losing submitted work
reason: All Planner checks finished at 8.75 seconds, then the packaged runtime did not exit within 21 seconds of SIGTERM during fixture cleanup and logged nothing, so the case exhausted 30 seconds. The last check had just dispatched auto-build work. This may be a real shutdown hang. Keep the recovery assertions and the cleanup.
removeWhen: Find why the packaged runtime ignores or stalls on SIGTERM after auto-build dispatch and fix it, then pass ten independent Linux runs within the existing 30 second allowance.

name: automatically recovers a CLI-started backend and restores the open project
reason: On Windows the app still reported `starting` when the 5 second recovery poll ended after the CLI-started backend restarted. The case normally takes 18 to 24 seconds of its 60 second allowance. Keep Linux and macOS coverage blocking and preserve the restored-project assertions.
removeWhen: Identify the slow restart phase on Windows and fix it, then pass ten independent Windows runs within the existing poll and test allowances.

name: turns a New session tab into the created session when the request ends after leaving the tab
reason: Timed out after 30 seconds filling the chat editor of a New session tab, before the held session request was sent, with no server errors; a re-run of the same job on the same commit passed. Keep the held-request and tab-switch assertions.
removeWhen: Find why the New session editor sometimes does not accept input, fix it, then pass ten independent Linux runs within the existing 30 second allowance.
